summary: Egress asymmetry causing UDP DNS truncation and intermittent TLS handshake stalls from private deploy
description: Issue summary: Customer FinScale reported recurring control-plane timeouts and downstream TLS handshake stalls after model artifact fetches and during streaming sessions. Impact: Several API requests from their private deployment intermittently fail to establish long-lived gRPC/TLS streams; token-level retries observed and increased latency for artifact pulls and heartbeat pings. Environment: Private deployment vpc-peering -> customer transit gateway -> shared egress NAT via customer firewall (prod - us-east-1). Observed behavior: DNS lookups for Redwood endpoints frequently return UDP truncated responses (TC bit set). Client falls back to TCP DNS, but outbound TCP to port 53 is intermittently blocked by the customer egress appliance, resulting in unresolved names or delayed resolution. Intermittent DNS resolution failures correlate with stalled TLS handshakes (client-side TLS 1.3 handshake timeout) when clients attempt to fetch presigned model URLs or open gRPC streams. Expected behavior: Untruncated DNS responses or allowed TCP53 fallback, and stable TLS handshake completion for artifact downloads and streaming sessions. Other notes: Issue appears correlated with asymmetric egress routing where DNS response path does not follow the same NAT device as request path, causing fragmented UDP responses to be dropped or path-MTU-dependent truncation.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer has VPC A (private deploy) peered to central transit gateway; egress to internet flows via NGFW cluster in another AZ.
2) From a serving node, perform repeated 'dig +short' queries against control-plane endpoint that returns large DNSSEC-enabled answers (simulate model catalog resolution).
3) Observe UDP responses with TC=1; verify tcp fallback attempt from client. If outbound TCP53 is blocked by NGFW, DNS resolution fails or times out.
4) Trigger a model artifact download or start a streaming session concurrently; observe TLS handshake stalls and gRPC stream timeouts correlated with the DNS failures.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 15:00 - Initial triage (Maya): Customer provided pcaps and traceroutes. Packet captures show DNS responses fragmented or larger than 512 bytes and TC set; many UDP fragments not reaching client IP due to reverse path via different NGFW pair.

2026-03-10 16:30 - Net team (Alejandro): Confirmed asymmetric return path. NAT pool on NGFW-A handles requests but responses take path through NGFW-B which does not have matching conntrack state, causing UDP fragments to be dropped. NGFW TCP port 53 policy is selectively enforced for unknown source ports and sometimes RSTs the connection.
2026-03-10 18:10 - Reproduced in staging by manipulating route tables to force egress through different NAT devices; observed identical DNS truncation and TCP53 reset behavior.

2026-03-11 09:00 - Hypothesis: Asymmetric egress + stateful NGFW causing UDP reassembly failure and blocking TCP DNS fallback, cascading to TLS handshake delays when name resolution stalls before presigned URL fetch or CDN selection.
temporary_workarounds: 1) Customer temporarily allowed TCP/53 egress between their NGFW pairs for the cluster CIDRs (worked around many failures within 10 minutes).
2) Short-term: Add explicit route to force symmetric egress via single NAT pair for serving node subnets (reduced occurrences).
3) On serving side, enable aggressive DNS caching and increase resolver timeout/retries to mask transient failures (mitigation only).
resolution_summary: Partial mitigation implemented: customer updated route tables to pin egress for affected subnets to a single NAT/NGFW pair to restore symmetric path. Customer changed NGFW policy to allow TCP/53 to Redwood control-plane CIDRs. These actions eliminated the majority of observed DNS truncation and TLS timeout events. Root cause remains design-level asymmetric egress with stateful inspection; follow-up required to harden control-plane resilience and document recommended network patterns.
next_steps: 1) Schedule joint change window with customer to make symmetric egress routes permanent (customer ops).
2) Internal: add guidance to Private Deploy runbook about egress symmetry and TCP/53 requirements for DNS fallback (owners: Networking docs team).
3) Engineering: consider adding more resilient name-resolution fallbacks in our agent (e.g., fallback to alternate resolvers, prefetch for presigned hostnames) - proposal in infra backlog.
4) Follow-up check in 72 hours after permanent routing change to confirm no reoccurrence and close ticket.
